findings.claim: `picocli.exit()` is used for the feature-disabled exit code and calls `System.exit()` directly. This hard-terminates the JVM and makes the following `return` unreachable.

verifier.reason: Picocli.exit (quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/cli/Picocli.java:203-207) calls System.exit only when the exit code is non-OK and either the launch mode is not test or a rebuild check is running. In test launch mode, and when a test subclass overrides exit (PicocliTest.java:85), the method returns normally, so the `return` at UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:49 and in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata is reachable and needed. The same exit pattern was already used at UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:57 before this patch.

findings.claim: The PR has no changelog or release-note entry for the exit-code renumbering, the new rolling-updates preview feature, or the requirement that update-compatibility now needs --features=rolling-updates.

verifier.reason: The patch only changes the guides (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc, docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc, docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc). It adds nothing under docs/documentation/release_notes or docs/documentation/upgrading. 26_2_0.adoc has no entry for the rolling-updates feature, and none covers the exit-code change in CompatibilityResult.java:34-35. That docs tree never mentions update-compatibility at all, so the command still looks unreleased.

findings.claim: The guide documents exit code 1 for a missing or corrupt metadata file, but the code throws PropertyException, which exits with code 2 (usage error).

verifier.reason: docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:122-123 says exit code 1 means the metadata file is missing or corrupt. But UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:80 and :90 throw PropertyException in those cases, and ExecutionExceptionHandler.java:44-50 turns a PropertyException into getInvalidInputExitCode. No exit-code mapper is set, so that falls back to exitCodeOnInvalidInput, which is picocli's default of 2 (ShortErrorMessageHandler.java:98-101).

findings.claim: Tests run only the 'update-compatibility metadata' subcommand with the feature disabled. The separate feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (lines 46-50) is never exercised.

verifier.reason: The only disabled-feature test is testFeatureNotEnabled (UpdateCommandDistTest.java:46-50), and it launches only the metadata subcommand. Every test that runs UpdateCompatibilityCheck passes ENABLE_FEATURE (lines 65, 81, 96, 105), so no test reaches the feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (lines 46-50 from the patch) or checks its FEATURE_DISABLED exit code.

findings.claim: The exit-code contract was renumbered (recreate 4->3, feature-disabled=4), but no test asserts either value. testFeatureNotEnabled and testIncompatible check only the message text.

verifier.reason: The patch changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and adds FEATURE_DISABLED=4 (CompatibilityResult.java:34-35). In UpdateCommandDistTest.java, testFeatureNotEnabled (line 236) and testIncompatible (lines 283, 292) only call assertError on message text, and the only exit-code check anywhere is assertEquals(0, ...) at line 75; no test refers to either constant or to the values 3 or 4.

findings.claim: The default-strategy test case returns before the rolling-updates feature flag is enabled, so the `null` branch no longer covers the rolling-update path.

verifier.reason: The early `if (updateStrategy == null) return kc;` at UpgradeTest.java:105-107 was already there before this patch. A null strategy goes to RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic (UpgradeLogicFactory.java:37-38), which picks rolling vs. recreate only by comparing images (RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic.java:53-57) and never checks the rolling-updates feature, so testCacheMaxCount with null still covers the rolling path.

findings.claim: The documentation table describes exit code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible'. Exit code 4 is also returned when the feature is disabled, with the message 'Unable to use this command...'. The table therefore conflates a disabled tool with a compatibility verdict and does not cover the metadata command returning 4.

verifier.reason: The table row the patch adds at docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:132-134 says exit code 4 means "The feature `rolling-updates` is disabled." That matches FEATURE_DISABLED = 4 in CompatibilityResult.java, so the table does not mix up a disabled tool with a compatibility result. The leading "Rolling Upgrade is not possible" wording and the missing mention of the metadata command are only minor wording issues.

findings.claim: The CAUTION documentation block (lines 446-450) says the Operator will fail unless the rolling-updates feature is enabled. The operator code does not check this feature, spec.update.strategy is not gated, and the default `<not set>` strategy works without it.

verifier.reason: The operator never checks the rolling-updates feature: UpgradeLogicFactory.java:36-42 picks the upgrade logic from spec.update.strategy alone (RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic when unset, AlwaysRecreateUpgradeLogic for Recreate), and nothing under operator/src/main references rolling-updates or ROLLING_UPDATES. Only the quarkus CLI update-compatibility commands get a feature check (UpdateCompatibilityCheck/UpdateCompatibilityMetadata run()), so the new CAUTION in advanced-configuration.adoc, which says the Operator will fail, is inaccurate.

findings.claim: UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() line 46 calls Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...) without ensuring Profile is initialized. This throws NullPointerException if Profile.getInstance() is null.

verifier.reason: Before `cmd.execute()` runs the command, Picocli.java:118/176 sets the parsed command to UpdateCompatibilityCheck and Picocli.java:128 calls `PropertyMappers.sanitizeDisabledMappers()`. That method creates the feature Profile if none exists, via `Environment.getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile()` (PropertyMappers.java:297-306), so `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` at UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46 will not throw a NullPointerException.

findings.claim: The same feature-disabled guard (isFeatureEnabled / printFeatureDisabled / exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) / return) is duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run() at lines 46-50 instead of being centralized in AbstractUpdatesCommand.

verifier.reason: The patch adds the same five-line guard (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ROLLING_UPDATES) → printFeatureDisabled() → picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED) → return) at lines 46-50 of both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(). AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:83-85 only centralizes the message helper, not the check itself.

findings.claim: The documentation macro hard-codes --features=rolling-updates after the user's parameters. This overrides features set via KC_FEATURES or keycloak.conf, and may not take effect on an --optimized image because features are build-time.

verifier.reason: The patch changes docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc:53 to `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility ${parameters} --features=rolling-updates`. That CLI value outranks KC_FEATURES and keycloak.conf, and PersistedConfigSource has ordinal 200, so it replaces any other features the user set. `features` is a build-time option, so with --optimized the check in Picocli.java:404-437 throws 'build time options have values that differ from what is persisted' unless the image was built with exactly that value.

findings.claim: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3, which changes the exit code that existing scripts consume.

verifier.reason: The patch changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult (change.patch:215-219) and reuses 4 for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` code. A script that treated 4 as 'recreate needed' would now misread the result, but the change is deliberate: it follows picocli exit-code conventions, is documented in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:128-134, and only affects the `ROLLING_UPDATES` feature, which is still in preview (Profile.java:136).
